title: Input boundary consistency condition
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-tape Turing machine with Boolean tape alphabet, let $v$ be a Boolean valuation on its atoms, let $\sigma$ be an optional machine state paired with an output register, and let $\rho$ specify read data. The condition is true if $\sigma$ has no state or the transition from its state reads the input tape at position zero. For a positive input position, it is true exactly when the input is clamped or the symbol encoded by the $t_n$ answer atom of type $a_j$, with no work tape selected and Boolean parameter false, is absent; for a negative position, replace that answer atom's Boolean parameter by true. The input is clamped when the input symbol in $\rho$ is absent and the $t_c$ answer symbol of type $a_1$, with no work tape selected and Boolean parameter true precisely when the input position is negative, is absent.
